verdict: Costco's net sales rose 7.5% to $61.0B as comparable sales climbed 5.2% — and with $1.17B of nearly cost-free membership fees on top, profit rose 13% to $1.80B, helped by a $100M tax benefit.

segments.name: Net sales
segments.note: Everything sold in the warehouses and online. Comparable sales rose 5.2% (7.1% adjusted for gas prices and currency), and e-commerce sales rose 13.0%.

segments.name: Membership fees
segments.note: Annual membership fees — almost pure profit, and the engine of Costco's earnings.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Running the warehouses, paying staff and the back office.

otherDetail: Interest income and other of $147M, less $37M of interest expense.
footerNote: Costco's merchandise costs include buying, freight and shrink (lost or damaged goods) — the direct cost of what's on the shelves. The quarter is 12 weeks, ended November 24, 2024.
follow100Note: Membership fees are only $1.88 of every $100 — but they arrive with almost no cost attached, which is why they cover about two-thirds of the $2.89 Costco kept as profit.

takeaways.title: Comparable sales still climbing
takeaways.text: Comparable sales rose 5.2% across the company (7.1% adjusted for gas prices and currency), and e-commerce sales jumped 13.0% — members kept spending in the warehouses and online.

takeaways.title: Membership fees keep growing
takeaways.text: Membership fee income rose 7.8% to $1.17B — steady, recurring income with no cost of goods attached to it. Costco ended the quarter with 897 warehouses.

takeaways.title: Profit up 13% with a tax assist
takeaways.text: Net income rose to $1.80B ($4.04 per share) from $1.59B a year ago. Operating income itself rose 10.7% to $2.20B, and this year's figure also included a $100M tax benefit linked to stock-based compensation.

oneTimers: A $100M tax benefit ($0.22 per diluted share) related to stock-based compensation flattered net income; a year ago the same benefit was $44M ($0.10 per share).
